title: HST WFC3/IR Calibrated Ramp-Stability Audit
question: After reconstructing accumulated electrons from UNITCORR-complete IMA count rates, is the residual late-versus-early ramp drift stable under declared pixel-selection choices?
gap: A correction and robustness audit of calibrated archive products; not an independent detector nonlinearity calibration.
dataMode: real public HST WFC3/IR IMA products
novelty: The original analysis treated ELECTRONS/S arrays as accumulated electrons. This release repairs the units and reframes the output as residual post-calibration ramp stability because NLINCORR is already COMPLETE.
methodology: Each IMA SCI and ERR plane is read with its BUNIT. ELECTRONS/S arrays are multiplied by the matching TIME.PIXVALUE to reconstruct accumulated electrons before any fit; unknown units fail closed. Exact file size and SHA-256 receipts are verified first. The analysis selects separated, deepest-read DQ-clean single pixels, excludes the zeroth read and flagged reads, and compares disjoint early and late weighted accumulation slopes. Eighteen declared designs cross 20 or 40 requested pixels, 3/5/7-pixel separation, and 0.4/0.5/0.6 early-read fractions. Because UNITCORR and NLINCORR are COMPLETE, the output is interpreted only as residual post-calibration ramp drift.
assumptions: IMA files follow the standard WFC3 MULTIACCUM convention: one (SCI, ERR, DQ, SAMP, TIME) extension quintet per read, EXTVER=1 is the last (deepest) read; ima_io.py raises DataSchemaError rather than assuming this silently if absent.
Single-pixel apertures and explicit centre separation avoid the overlapping 3x3 measurements used by the earlier release.

WFC3/IR data-quality bit definitions (HOTPIX=16, SPIKE=1024, SATPIXEL=256, DATAREJECT=8192, HIGH_CURVATURE=16384, etc.) were verified directly against the real spacetelescope/hstcal source rather than assumed from memory.
limitations: Only two of three selected exposures have at least six positive-time reads; this cannot support a population-level interval.

The IMA files are already corrected by calwf3 with NLINCORR=COMPLETE. Residual drift cannot be identified uniquely with detector nonlinearity and may include scene, pointing, persistence, background, or other calibration effects.
The selected bright pixels are deterministic descriptive samples, not independent draws from the WFC3/IR detector population.
This release relies on official STScI WFC3 data-structure and calibration documentation for the unit and calibration-state interpretation; it does not claim a literature-calibrated detector model.
reports/report.tex could not be compiled to PDF in this environment (no local LaTeX toolchain); only structural completeness was verified.
